26: Optional encumbrance rules: threshold based on Strength + Body, and a single armor item can be ignored for encumbrance.
27: Optional alternative conjuring drain (Street Magic p. 31, Unwired p. 39): half the Force/Rating plus the opposing hits, for spirits and sprites.
28: Optional knockdown rule: damage can knock the target down, configurable for every attack or gel rounds only, with a Body modifier and an automatic threshold.
29: Visibility modifiers: set lighting and obscurant per scene; attacks, spellcasting and visual Perception tests get a pre-calculated visibility modifier based on the best available vision mode, editable per roll. Self and touch spells are exempt.

Vision modes (low-light, thermographic, ultrasound, flare compensation) are managed in their own list on the Bio & Contacts tab, the NPC sheet and the vehicle sheet. Metatype vision (powers and qualities such as Low-Light Vision) is picked up automatically, and every mode can be deactivated and reactivated. The Chummer character import adds vision options from cyberware and fills the metatype from a matching Metatype item in the world or a compendium.
Perception tests can choose the sense (sight, hearing, smell/taste, touch), each with its own bonus, set on the Modifiers tab or via Active Effects.
New status "Astral Perception": while active, no visibility modifier applies.

Area spells: the radius equals the Force in meters and can be changed by 1 m per withheld die in the Force dialog (Street Magic p. 160). One success test applies to all targets, and the roll card shows Force and radius.

Area combat and illusion spells place their area as a scene region; tokens inside become targets and can be unchecked in a list before the roll. Can be turned off in the flow settings or per cast in the Force dialog; without a placement the spell hits the marked targets after confirmation. Players who may not create regions get theirs created by the GM.
Spells on several targets request all resistance tests at once and summarise the results on one chat card. Spells with range Self always target the caster.
The spell sheet has a separate Area checkbox next to the range; existing spells with range Area are converted automatically.
